parsed.explanation: No trans-specific offence, no sodomy law, and no documented police targeting, border/facility/custody universal exposure, or trans-specific violence against visitors. Positives are limited: trans people appear in traditional costumes at temples/ceremonies and as entertainment, suggesting some familiarity, but not documented acceptance as gender identity. Negatives extrapolated from thin, mostly LGBTI-wide record: state tolerates people only unless they campaign or are deemed publicly immodest, societal discrimination was reported prevalent, censorship and social-media crackdown, one advocacy group, and no documented visitor-facing remedy or protective enforcement for discrimination/assault. Resident-facing absence of anti-discrimination law is not itself visitor exposure. This sits a step below documented acceptance-with-working-recourse, without reaching universal-exposure or organised-targeting tiers.
